The proof adds that hypothesis. Under the written definition, columns can be dependent, so the claimed independent-column property and later sums of independent random matrices do not follow.

issues.failure_explanation: Conditioning on the truncation event changes the distributions and expectations of the summands. Even if the product-form event preserves conditional independence, the proof has not shown that the conditional mean remains $\ell I_r$ or has minimum eigenvalue $\ell$. Matrix Chernoff therefore cannot be applied conditionally with the unconditional parameter $\mu_{\min}=\ell$. The same unsupported step is repeated for the upper tail and in the subspace-embedding proof.
